at spekulere.explanation: "At spekulere" means "to speculate / wonder". To name what you wonder about, add "på" (about): "Jeg spekulerer på det" (I wonder about that). To say you invest money in something, add "i" (in): "spekulere i aktier" (to speculate in shares).

at spilde.explanation: "At spilde" means "to waste / spill". To say liquid runs out by accident, use it with the liquid: "Jeg spildte vand på bordet" (I spilled water on the table). To say you waste something, use it with the thing: "Vi må ikke spilde mad" (We must not waste food).

at spilde tid.explanation: "At spilde tid" means "to waste time". To say what wastes your time, add "på" (on): "Jeg spilder tid på telefonen" (I waste time on the phone). The verb "at spilde" (to waste) also works without "tid" (time) to mean "to spill": "Jeg spildte kaffe" (I spilled coffee).

at spille.explanation: "At spille" means "to play". To say you play a game, a sport or an instrument, use it with that word: "Vi spiller fodbold" (We play soccer). To say an actor plays a part, use it with the part: "Hun spiller en prinsesse" (She plays a princess). To say children play for fun, use "at lege" (to play) instead: "Børnene leger i haven" (The children are playing in the garden).

at spille en rolle.explanation: "At spille en rolle" means "to play a role". To say someone acts a part on stage, use it with the place: "Hun spiller en rolle i skolens teater" (She plays a role in the school theater). To say something does not matter, use it with "ikke nogen" (not any): "Prisen spiller ikke nogen rolle" (The price does not matter).

at spille fodbold.explanation: "At spille fodbold" means "to play soccer". The word "fodbold" is built from "fod" (foot) and "bold" (ball). The verb "at spille" (to play) works for other sports too: "spille håndbold" (to play handball).

at spise.explanation: "At spise" means "to eat". To say you eat at a restaurant, add "ude" (out): "Vi spiser ude i aften" (We are eating out tonight). To say you drink, use "at drikke" (to drink) instead: "Jeg drikker vand" (I drink water).

at sponsorere.explanation: "At sponsorere" means "to sponsor". To say a company pays for an event, use it with the event: "Firmaet sponsorerer kampen" (The company sponsors the match). The person or company that does it is "en sponsor" (a sponsor).

at spore.explanation: "At spore" means "to track / trace". It is built on "et spor" (a trail or footprint). To say you trace where a call came from, use it with the call: "spore et opkald" (to trace a call).

at sprede.explanation: "At sprede" means "to spread". To say something spreads by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Rygtet spreder sig" (The rumor spreads). To say someone spreads something, leave out "sig": "Han spreder rygtet" (He spreads the rumor).

at springe.explanation: "At springe" means "to jump". To say you skip a page, add "over" (over): "Jeg springer en side over" (I skip a page).

at springe over.explanation: "At springe over" means "to skip". To say you leave out a meal, use it with the meal: "Jeg springer frokosten over" (I skip lunch). To say you jump across something, use it with the thing: "Hunden sprang over hegnet" (The dog jumped over the fence).

at sprænge.explanation: "At sprænge" means "to blow up". To say explosives destroy something, use it with the thing: "at sprænge en bro" (to blow up a bridge). To say you go over a limit, use it with the limit: "at sprænge budgettet" (to blow the budget).

at sprøjte.explanation: "At sprøjte" means "to spray". The noun "en sprøjte" (a syringe) is spelled the same way: "Lægen giver mig en sprøjte" (The doctor gives me an injection).

at spytte.explanation: "At spytte" means "to spit". To say where you spit, add "på" (on): "spytte på gulvet" (spit on the floor). To say a dragon breathes out fire, use it with the fire: "Dragen spytter ild" (The dragon spits fire).

at spænde.explanation: "At spænde" means "to tighten / fasten". To tell someone to pull a strap tight, say: "Spænd remmen" (Tighten the strap). To say you tense your body, use it with the muscles: "Jeg spænder musklerne" (I tense my muscles).

at spøge.explanation: "At spøge" means "to joke". To say you are not serious, add "kun" (only): "Jeg spøger kun" (I am only joking). To say a ghost is in a place, use "det" (it) and the place: "Det spøger i huset" (The house is haunted).

at spørge.explanation: "At spørge" means "to ask". To ask a person about something, add "om" (about): "Jeg spørger ham om vejen" (I ask him about the way). To ask for something you want, use "at bede om" (to ask for) instead: "Jeg beder om en kop kaffe" (I ask for a cup of coffee).

at spørge om.explanation: "At spørge om" means "to ask about". To ask about a thing, put it after "om" (about): "spørge om prisen" (ask about the price). To ask for something you need, use it the same way: "spørge om hjælp" (ask for help).

at spørge om vej.explanation: "At spørge om vej" means "to ask for directions", literally "to ask about way". To stop a stranger and ask, say: "Undskyld, må jeg spørge om vej?" (Excuse me, may I ask for directions?)

at stabilisere.explanation: "At stabilisere" means "to stabilize". To say something steadies by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Priserne stabiliserer sig" (The prices stabilize).

at stadfæste.explanation: "At stadfæste" means "to confirm / uphold". To say a court keeps a decision, use it with the decision: "Retten stadfæstede dommen" (The court upheld the verdict).

at stamme.explanation: "At stamme" means "to stutter / come from". To say someone stutters, use it alone: "Han stammer, når han er nervøs" (He stutters when he is nervous). To say where something comes from, add "fra" (from): "Min familie stammer fra Jylland" (My family comes from Jutland).

at standse.explanation: "At standse" means "to stop". To say a vehicle comes to a halt, use it with the vehicle: "Bilen standsede foran huset" (The car stopped in front of the house). To say you quit a habit, use "at holde op" (to quit) instead: "Jeg holder op med at ryge" (I am quitting smoking).

at starte.explanation: "At starte" means "to start". To say an event begins, use it with the time: "Vi starter i morgen" (We start tomorrow). To say a machine will not run, use it with the machine: "Bilen starter ikke" (The car will not start). To say a lesson begins, "at begynde" (to begin) works too: "Timen begynder klokken ni" (The lesson begins at nine).
